d: A long-standing goiter in which several nodules have become autonomous, making hormone without TSH; uptake is patchy and high, and iodine loads can tip it into thyrotoxicosis.
A nuclear test measuring the share of an oral iodine tracer that the thyroid traps; high uptake means new synthesis, and low uptake means a leak or an outside source.
The IgG autoantibody of Graves disease that binds and activates the TSH receptor on follicular cells and on orbital and pretibial fibroblasts; it crosses the placenta.
Autoimmune swelling of orbital fat and extraocular muscles from fibroblast glycosaminoglycan deposition and fat formation, causing exophthalmos and diplopia; smoking and radioactive iodine worsen it.
Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis after a viral illness: a painful, tender gland, high ESR, giant-cell granulomas, low uptake and a hyper, then hypo, then euthyroid course.
Painless lymphocytic thyroiditis within a year of delivery, often with anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies; it leaks stored hormone, shows low uptake and may leave permanent hypothyroidism.

A thionamide that inhibits thyroid peroxidase and peripheral 5'-deiodinase; preferred in the first trimester and in thyroid storm, it carries risks of hepatotoxicity, agranulocytosis and ANCA vasculitis.
